excerpt: Portea Medical provides home healthcare in India: nurses, physiotherapy, attendants, lab tests and medical equipment. FY25 results, funding and alternatives.
content:
Portea Medical is an Indian home healthcare company. It sends doctors, nurses, physiotherapists and trained attendants to patients' homes, and offers lab tests, vaccination, elder care, mother-and-baby care, diabetes care, critical care at home, counselling and the rental or sale of medical equipment. Its website calls it India's home healthcare pioneer since 2013 and claims more than 20 lakh (2 million) patients served, over 100 hospital partners and 135 cities. Patients book online or through a phone line, a clinical team assesses the need, and Portea matches a professional to the case.

Meena Ganesh is Portea's founder and chief executive, according to TechCrunch. Accel led its Series B, a $37.5 million round in which the International Finance Corporation and Qualcomm Ventures also took part, and in November 2017 TechCrunch reported a $26 million Series C led by Sabre Partners and MEMG CDC, bringing its total to about $72.5 million at the time. Entrackr, citing TheKredible, puts total funding at nearly $123 million, with Accel and Ventureast as lead investors.

Entrackr reported in January 2026 that Portea's revenue from operations grew 15% to Rs 160 crore in FY25 (the year to March 2025), while its loss fell 49% to Rs 19 crore. Services such as nursing, physiotherapy and lab tests made up 59% of operating income (Rs 95 crore), and sales of products such as oxygen concentrators, BiPAP machines and nebulisers brought in Rs 56 crore.

Portea does not publish a price list. Charges depend on the service, the city and how long care is needed, and are quoted when you book.

This profile is put together from the company's own pages and published reporting, checked on 15 October 2026. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.
